### Historical audit

**Source:** S0080, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_regression_guidance/C1/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 is available; citations below refer to this file.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, JSONL line 19, chars [0,141849) | The stated goal was to reconstruct one RGB indoor photograph with separate meshes and matching camera/framing. The student interpreted it as a ship compartment; that semantic interpretation is not independently verified here. |
| Same event, initial student program | The code constructs multiple groups: architecture, three bunks, two foreground cabinets, lockers, chair, bench, wall equipment, pipes and lamps. It groups chair parts and uses explicit positions for supports, but grouping and intended contact do not establish physical connection or rendered visibility. Objects are predominantly colored primitives; no image texture is used. |
| Same event, step 1 result and step 2 program | The runner reported step 1 `ok: true` and a saved render. The student described the lamp as too low, post too central and rear furniture too small, then hypothesized a camera correction. It changed lens 23.5 to 31.5 and the target, while retaining geometry; it also enabled denoising, so the revision was not literally camera-only. Step 2 also reported `ok: true` and a saved render. |
| Same event, step 3 program and result | The student claimed improved post framing but remaining lamp/bunk differences. It hypothesized excessive ambient and frontal light, then darkened colors, reduced world and area lighting, adjusted roughness and added lamp emission. It preserved the step 2 camera and coded object placement. Step 3 reported `ok: true` and a saved render. The logs show 16 rendered samples despite code requesting 32; the cause is not established. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 20, chars [0,4496); `model_response`, line 21, chars [0,377) | The final session had reference and three render image inputs, was read-only, and recorded zero tool calls. It completed and responded `DONE`. The task instructions say the last successful build is submitted automatically; no separate submission confirmation is visible. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No distinct teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk. The repeated runner instruction to compare renders and change one parameter family was actually included in the student's input; the subsequent camera and appearance revisions are consistent with its adoption, though causation cannot be isolated. The student's own observations and hypotheses show iterative exploration across three executions, not independent verification of their accuracy.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Execution/render success is reported for all three builds; overall reconstruction correctness remains **unknown**, not formally verified. The images themselves are not visible in this audit. Thus object coverage, pose, occlusion, material resemblance, contact and camera/light quality cannot be independently checked. The student's landmark estimates and appearance diagnosis remain hypotheses, including whether darker lighting improved the match. No algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is shown in the visible chunk.

**Transferable lesson:** separating camera and appearance experiments and preserving grouped geometry makes changes easier to attribute, subject to incidental render-setting changes. **Task-specific:** the ship-compartment inventory, landmark estimates and chosen lighting are interpretations of this particular unseen image, not verified scene facts.
